meta.title: Ondra Vision
meta.description: Image understanding, OCR, object localisation and video frame sampling (handbook §9.4, P1, reuse tier). The handbook gives one and a half sentences: image understanding / OCR / object localisation / video frame sampling, pluggable provider, off by default. The corpus adds: pluggable providers (OpenAI-compatible cloud / local Ollama / Qwen), off by default, wired to privacy with an outbound prompt. So this package only wires, configures and degrades: not one line of inference is written here, the recognition belongs to the provider, and this package owns request shaping, timeouts, result shaping and outbound permission. Three judgements are hard-wired. First, off by default: sending one image out equals sending the user's screen to someone else, and a screenshot may hold chat logs, an ID card or a payslip. Second, outbound needs someone to say whether it may go: if privacy is present its verdict rules, with allow, ask and deny kept distinct; without privacy, cloud is refused unless explicitly opened. Third, every failure returns a reason code quietly, never throws and never invents content: if it cannot see, it says so, because a guessed description becomes a false memory. The three providers differ in exactly two places (path and image field), so they share one implementation under the merge rule. Boxes are always normalised to 0-1; if a model answers in pixels, they are converted with the real dimensions, and if that conversion is impossible the whole batch is rejected rather than guessed. This package draws no UI, creates no session, writes no memory and installs no timers; ingestion belongs to O-128, outbound compliance to O-076, and the interface to the application shell.
